paragraphs: Apple’s new Siri Remote adds a long-requested feature that makes it easier to track down the little controller when it goes missing… which you know it will. And you don’t have to buy the company’s new Apple TV 4K to get it.
The updated remote, announced Tuesday alongside Apple’s latest streaming box, adds an audible alert sound to make the device more findable. And it has Precision Finding, too.
The Siri Remote (4th Generation) is sold separately, so owners of older Apple TV models can upgrade to it.

It is a remarkably universal human experience to settle in for a relaxing evening, only to discover that the TV remote has mysteriously vanished. Whether tucked deep between couch cushions, left on a kitchen counter during a snack run or accidentally swept under a pile of mail, remotes have an uncanny ability to disappear right when they are needed most.

You can stop playing Hide-and-Seek with your remote… if you get the Apple TV 4K version introduced on Tuesday. With the Find My application, users can play a sound to help find the device nearby, a particularly useful addition for a Siri Remote.
Previous versions offered only proximity notifications using on-screen indicators (“far,” “near,” “here”). An audible notification should be much more useful.
And that’s not all. Precision Finding in the Find My app pulls up an arrow that points directly toward the device. Or the app can show the accessory on a map if it gets really lost.

Note that only the newest version of the Siri Remote includes a speaker. And Precision Finding requires the latest version paired with an iPhone Duo, iPhone Air or an iPhone 17 or newer model with UWB.
